title: A Guide to Nepal Physics Olympiad
why: Written by Laxman Bist, Nabin Kalauni, Sandesh Parajuli — top-3 of NePhO 2018, Nepal's team at IPhO 2018 Lisbon. Explicitly "organized as per the syllabus of NePhO." Every chapter = Key Concepts & Formulae → Bridging Problem → Level 1 problems → Level 2 problems → IPhO problems → Supplementary problems, all with solutions. Sources cited inside: Morin, Irodov, Gnädig, Sears & Zemansky. Released Oct 2023, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

title: Jaan Kalda — "Recommended list of problems"
why: The most respected curated olympiad problem list in the world, hand-picked by an IPhO organiser and sorted by topic: Mechanics (incl. celestial), Electromagnetism, Thermodynamics, Optics, Relativity, Quantum. Each entry annotated with why it teaches something (e.g. "IPhO-1991-Pr1 — this will teach you the basics of the collision of bodies"). Start here before touching raw archives.

title: Kalda — "Formulas for IPhO" (ver 1.1)
why: The de-facto standard IPhO formula sheet. Also in Spanish, Japanese, Portuguese, Indonesian, Estonian — no Nepali version exists (Gap I-3).

title: Official IPhO Syllabus (accepted Astana 2014, amended Mumbai 2015)
why: Section-by-section: 2.2 Mechanics (kinematics / statics / dynamics / celestial mechanics), 2.3 Electromagnetic fields (basic concepts / integral forms of Maxwell's equations / interaction of matter with fields / circuits), 2.4 Oscillations & waves (single oscillator / waves / interference & diffraction / EM waves in matter), plus thermodynamics, modern physics, and experimental skills incl. error analysis.

title: Errors and their Propagation — Kafle & Limbu
why: Foundation for the mandatory "Experimental uncertainty & Data analysis" syllabus section. 4 pp.

title: Graphing for NePhO — Prabhakar Kafle & Sanam Limbu
why: Explicitly built for NePhO. Opens with a NePhO Pre-selection 2017 graph question. Graphing is a named scoring skill in the official NePhO syllabus. 5 pp.

title: Mechanics for NePhO — Dinesh Kandel (IPhO 2011 Bronze, Nepal)
why: "Preparation Materials FOR IPhO — NePhO, Nepal Physical Society." Contains an actual NePhO 2011 selection-test problem (falling-raindrop model) worked up to competition standard. The deepest Nepal-authored mechanics treatment available.

title: Significant Figures and Rounding — Kafle & Limbu
why: NePhO papers state: "Marks will not be deducted for incorrect answers but deducted for improper significant figures." This is free marks most Nepali students lose. 2 pp.

title: AAPT — U.S. Physics Team exams (F=ma, USAPhO, USAPhO Plus), all years + solutions
why: F=ma is a 25-question/75-min MCQ round — perfect timed-drill material for NePhO Section A; USAPhO is free-response at NePhO-Final/IPhO difficulty.

title: An Introduction to Error Analysis — John R. Taylor
accessNote: Unreachable from some networks (India-hosted mirror; times out abroad). Search title to find it; or buy.
why: Kafle: "if you want in-depth knowledge from the very beginning (which will be required eventually in IPhO), the best material should be John R. Taylor's." The definitive text.

title: BdPhO National Round papers, Category C
why: The National Round of BdPhO ≈ NePhO Final Round in difficulty and is freely downloadable (unlike INPhO).

title: BdPhO Past Papers — 13th BdPhO, Category C (Higher Secondary)
accessNote: LIVE but JavaScript-only SPA — needs a browser; not scrapeable. Category A/B/C correspond to school tiers.
why: Bangladesh's olympiad has an identical ladder shape to what you want: Selection Round → Regional Round (multiple question sets) → National Round, with Category C = higher secondary = Nepal's Grade 11–12. Difficulty sits right between NePhO Round 1 and Round 2. The single best volume-drill source for South Asian students.

title: Curriculum Development Centre (CDC) — Digital Library portal
accessNote: Same geo-slowness. Accessible from within Nepal.
why: Entry point for all NEB textbooks & curricula.

title: Gulf Physics Olympiads (GPhO)
why: ABEGS-organised; 3 editions with problems.

title: HBCSE (India) — Past Papers index (NSEP + INPhO, 2008–2025, English and Hindi)
accessNote: Index ✅ LIVE, but individual PDFs 404 from non-Indian IPs (geo-restricted). Use from within Nepal/India or via archive.org.
why: India's national olympiad papers with official model solutions. INPhO is ~1 notch above NePhO Final Round; NSEP is ~NePhO Round 1. Hindi versions help Nepali students more comfortable in Devanagari.

title: HRK (5th ed.) — complete MCQ answer key (Kevin Zhou Ch. 1–17 + Physoly community Vol. 2)
accessNote: Kevin Zhou's /handouts/ index returns 404; the direct PDF and the Google Doc are the live routes
why: Halliday–Resnick–Krane is the rigorous edition; this makes it self-study-able.

title: HyperPhysics (Georgia State University)
why: Fast concept cross-referencing; excellent for filling holes before you touch olympiad problems.

title: Jaan Kalda — (ver 0.5)
why: Interference, diffraction, polarization. The only free olympiad-grade optics handout identified; there is no Nepali equivalent at any level.

title: Jaan Kalda — (ver 1.2)
why: DC/AC circuit theory at olympiad depth — covers the Kirchhoff / thermoelectric / AC circuits syllabus items the Nepal guide omits.

title: Jaan Kalda — (ver 1.2)
why: Rotation, rigid bodies, gravitation, oscillations — the Round-1 mechanics blocks missing from the Nepal guide.

title: Jaan Kalda — study guide (ver 0.87)
why: IPhO-level thermodynamics with hints. Bridges NePhO Round 1 thermo → Round 2 → IPhO.

title: Kalda — "A short introduction to nonlinear waves"
why: Stretch material for IPhO-bound students.

title: Kalda — Complete study-guide index (all of the above + translations + terms of use)
why: Master page for S31–S40.

title: Kalda — Kinematics (ver 2.0)
Kalda — Quantum Mechanics (ver 0.4)
Kalda — Theory of Relativity (Siim Ainsaar, ver 0.6)
why: Directly serves the "basics of special relativity" in the NePhO Final Round syllabus.

title: MIT OCW 8.01SC Classical Mechanics
why: Full first-year mechanics with problem sets + exams. The standard bridge from board physics to olympiad mechanics.

title: MIT OCW 8.02 Physics II — Electricity & Magnetism
why: Covers magnetic field, magnetic properties of materials, electromagnetic induction, alternating currents — the entire §2 of the official Final-Selection syllabus, which no Nepali resource covers.

title: MIT OCW 8.03SC Physics III — Vibrations and Waves
why: Covers mechanical waves, acoustic phenomena, interference, diffraction, polarization — the entire §1 of the official Final-Selection syllabus, also uncovered by Nepali material.

title: Nordic-Baltic Physics Olympiad (NBPhO) problems
why: Kalda's own regional olympiad; the Est-Fin problems on his recommended list come from here.
